findings.reason: The authentic original image contains only the formulas and proof. A pair of step graphs materially clarifies why the right-continuous CDF takes its upper value at the jump, and why the moving positive jump leaves the value at zero unequal to the limit CDF. This is a warranted explanatory addition under the expanded diagram scope.
findings.action: Added two schematic CDF panels in a final Remarks section, outside the unchanged rigorous Counterexample proof.

correction: Appended explanatory Remarks and a TikZ plot of F_n and F with open lower and filled upper jump endpoints; preserved all original bytes, including publication status and protected metadata.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Functions F_n,F: R -> [0,1], the CDFs of delta_(1/n) and delta_0.
diagram_math_checks.check: By local F2 and step 1.1, a point mass has CDF 0 below its mass location and 1 at or above that location. The left panel has its jump at positive 1/n, the right panel at 0; horizontal scale is explicitly schematic.

Step 3.1 states F_n(t)=1_{t>=1/n} and F(t)=1_{t>=0}. Each panel therefore excludes its lower endpoint and includes its upper endpoint; no vertical graph segment is drawn. The dashed guide in the left panel is gray, separate from the cyan graph.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Failure at zero and agreement at continuity points
diagram_math_checks.check: The left zero-level branch contains t=0 since 1/n>0, so F_n(0)=0; the right upper endpoint is (0,1), so F(0)=1. For t<0 both CDFs equal zero; for fixed t>0, n>1/t gives F_n(t)=1=F(t). Thus only the limiting jump obstructs pointwise convergence.
Unchanged step 2.1 computes integrals as f(1/n) -> f(0) for every bounded continuous f, invoking F1. The diagram and caption add no proof premise.
